title: Flat band and Bulk-Boundary correspondence in a non-Hermitian trimerized lattice model with generic boundary conditions
authors: Supriyo Ghosh, Pijush K. Ghosh, Shreekantha Sil
abstract: We consider a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger(SSH)-type trimer model with next-nearest-neighbor(NNN) interaction and balanced loss-gain(BLG) to study the combined effect of lattice symmetries, topology, non-hermiticity and general boundary conditions(GBC)on the existence of flat band and the nature of Bulk-Boundary correspondence(BBC). We derive the necessary and sufficient conditions for the existence of an entirely real spectrum under the periodic boundary condition(PBC). The exact expressions for the compact localized states(CLS) and energy eigenvalues corresponding to flat bands are derived analytically under the PBC. We establish topological phase transitions(TPT) for PT-symmetry and pseudo-chiral symmetry through the computation of the Zak phase and sub-lattice Zak phase, respectively. The Hamiltonian under the open boundary condition(OBC) is studied numerically, and edge states are observed in the topologically non-trivial phase, thereby establishing the non-hermitian BBC. The CLS exists in both bulk and the boundary for systems having only pseudo-chiral symmetry, and an additional PT-symmetry destroys the CLS at the boundary. We generalize a known formalism to study the same Hamiltonian under GBC, and derive analytic expressions for the energy and eigenstates for a class of boundary conditions in parametric ranges which admit flat band under the PBC. The edge states for these boundary conditions, including the OBC, are obtained analytically in the topologically non-trivial phase, thereby establishing BBC. The non-hermitian skin effect(NHSE) is seen in the model with reciprocal bulk interaction and strongly non-reciprocal boundary terms. The winding number based on spectral topology is computed analytically.
summary: This paper analyzes a non-Hermitian trimerized lattice model to understand how lattice symmetries and boundary conditions affect topological properties. It establishes the non-Hermitian Bulk-Boundary Correspondence and derives analytical results for edge states under general boundary conditions. The findings are crucial for designing artificial quantum systems with controlled topological edge states.
main_problem: The study investigates the combined effects of lattice symmetries, non-Hermiticity, and general boundary conditions on the existence of flat bands and the nature of the Bulk-Boundary Correspondence (BBC).
main_result: The authors establish non-Hermitian BBC in the trimerized lattice model and derive analytic expressions for edge states under general boundary conditions, showing how symmetry dictates the presence of localized states.
method: The research employs analytical derivations for spectral properties under periodic and general boundary conditions, alongside numerical simulations to observe edge states and topological phase transitions.
model_or_system: The model is a Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH)-type trimer model incorporating next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) interactions and balanced loss-gain (BLG) terms, making it non-Hermitian.
key_observables: Flat bands (Compact Localized States, CLS), Topological Phase Transitions (TPT) via Zak phases, Bulk-Boundary Correspondence (BBC), and the non-Hermitian Skin Effect (NHSE).
important_parameters: BLG interaction strength, NNN interaction strength, and the specific parameters defining the general boundary conditions (GBC).
main_assumptions: The analysis generalizes previous work by extending the formalism to include general boundary conditions (GBC) beyond simple open or periodic boundaries.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the context implies figures showing energy spectra, topological invariants (Zak phases), and edge state localization.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system under PBC to find conditions for real spectra and derive CLS, then extends the analysis to OBC and finally generalizes the formalism to study the Hamiltonian under arbitrary GBC.
why_interesting: The work bridges concepts from topological physics (SSH models, topology) with non-Hermitian physics (loss/gain, non-Hermiticity), which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems and engineered photonic/electronic lattices.
